Text: For all benign states and policies, V_pi^M'(s)>=V_pi^M(s); the identity-remapping base case claims equality.

Kind: paraphrase

Location: Main §3 p2 Eq1; main §4.2 p5 Eq10

Text: Eq1 applies coefficients (1-beta),beta to T' entries even though Eq10 defines T' as the already weighted full kernel.

assumptions: Finite benign states {low,b,high}, two actions {target,non-target}, deterministic self loops under either action; disjoint bijective poisoned copy.
Complete benign reward function R(s,a,s')=r(s'), with r(low)=0, r(b)=1/2, r(high)=1, including impossible cross-component transitions. Extrema are attained on actual self loops.
beta=gamma=1/2; policy always non-target, so phi argmax is never used on policy.
Grant normalized Eq10 full transition kernel in place of doubly weighted Eq1; grant benign successor pullback when R is called on a poisoned successor.
Use prior-reward domain [0,1] explicitly assumed by Eq15, not literal unrestricted reals.
Use the forward-consistent incoming reward for future tau in the benign-to-poison correction; original incoming and corrected received incoming readings agree here.

Entry rewards 0,3/4,1 satisfy c=r+gamma[r-tau(non-target,r,c)]. All 72 state/action/successor triples satisfy the reward bound for every admissible prior reward; endpoint enumeration is supported by monotonicity, not a finite-grid-only claim.

Central operative previous-reward histories {0,1/2,3/4} are closed and yield tau=0. If initial distribution is needed, uniform benign states makes both original extrema occur with positive probability.
S and Sp are disjoint; delta is bijective; T and T' are stochastic rows; beta lies strictly between0 and1.
Attack enabled, caller asr<1 and sampling budget allow selection.
Finite categorical logits give index0 positive probability, and a positive selected score leads to the target action.
Cached empirical L=0,U=1 have already been observed in earlier data; a first constant batch alone would not establish them.
Three chronological rewards all1/2 and gamma1/2; selected index0.
